concepts.title: Transverse and Longitudinal Waves
concepts.definition: A wave carries energy through a medium without carrying the medium along. In transverse waves the particles vibrate across the travel direction -- ripples on a string -- while in longitudinal waves they push back and forth along it, forming compressions and rarefactions like sound in air.
concepts.key_idea: The disturbance travels, the medium stays -- the particle motion direction relative to the wave classifies it.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph207.txt lines 30-140 (sections 14.1, 14.2 progressive waves, transverse and longitudinal waves, compressions and rarefactions, crests and troughs)

solution_steps.explain: Every wave moves energy through the medium in one overall direction.
Particles crossing the travel direction make it transverse; particles oscillating along it make it longitudinal.
Transverse waves show crests and troughs; longitudinal waves show compressions and rarefactions sweeping forward.

concepts.title: Wave Parameters: Wavelength, Frequency and Speed
concepts.definition: A travelling harmonic wave is described by amplitude, wavelength (the distance between like phases), frequency (oscillations per second at a fixed spot) and speed. These lock together: the wave speed equals frequency times wavelength, because in one period the pattern advances exactly one wavelength.
concepts.key_idea: Speed is frequency times wavelength -- the universal currency note of all wave motion.

concepts.title: Speed of a Wave on a String
concepts.definition: A string's wave speed comes from its tension and its mass per unit length: the square root of tension divided by linear density. Tighter strings carry waves faster, heavier strings slower -- which is why guitars tune by adjusting tension and use different gauges for different pitches.
concepts.key_idea: Restore the flat string fast (tension) but drag its mass along (density) -- their ratio sets the speed.

solution_steps.explain: The ratio of stretching force to mass per length has the units of speed squared.
The root is the wave speed along the string.

concepts.title: Speed of Sound in a Gas
concepts.definition: Sound races through a gas as longitudinal pressure waves, with speed equal to the square root of the ratio of the elastic property to the inertia property -- gamma times pressure over density for an ideal gas. Newton's isothermal guess underestimates it; Laplace's adiabatic correction gives the right, temperature-dependent value.
concepts.key_idea: Stiffness over inertia under a root, with gamma for the adiabatic squeeze -- sound speeds up in hotter, lighter gases.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph207.txt lines 330-430 (section 14.5 the speed of a travelling wave continued: speed of sound in gases, Newton's and Laplace's formulae, effect of temperature)

solution_steps.explain: The adiabatic modulus is gamma times the pressure.
Dividing by the density and taking the root yields the sound speed.

concepts.title: Superposition, Standing Waves and Harmonics
concepts.definition: Overlapping waves simply add their displacements -- the principle of superposition. Two identical waves running opposite ways on a string add to a standing wave with fixed nodes and antinodes, and a string pinned at both ends accepts only frequencies that fit a whole number of half wavelengths: the harmonics.
concepts.key_idea: Nodes are where waves cancel forever; the allowed frequencies are whole-number multiples of the fundamental half-wave fit.

solution_steps.explain: The chosen harmonic n fits n half wavelengths into the string length.
Multiplying n by speed over the full out-and-back length gives that harmonic's frequency.

concepts.title: Beats and the Doppler Effect
concepts.definition: Two tones of nearly equal frequency played together wax and wane at the difference frequency -- beats -- useful for tuning instruments. When source or listener moves, the received frequency shifts (the Doppler effect), rising on approach and falling on retreat, the physics behind sirens and astronomical redshifts.
concepts.key_idea: Beats are the difference frequency made audible; Doppler shifts trace the closing or opening speed.
